Area.evidence_source: Thus, church attendance is perceived as protective during life crises. Similarly, a woman wished she had prayed about her problems "I feel it [suicide attempt] … it will not help me. I should have taken it to the Lord in prayer" (woman 1). It appears that for this woman, not surrendering her challenges to God to take control was a personal shortcoming. As her challenges seemed overwhelming and she could not bear them any longer she found suicide as the way out. Osafo and colleagues (2013) found that one way in which people could be resilient during crises is through religion; suicidal behaviour "was perceived as a consequence of having disregarded the utility of religious faith" (p. 6). They argued that prayer seems to create some level of relationship between an individual and the divine in which the person perceives that help could come from God during crises. Consequently, God is conceptualised as a significant form of social support and this could relieve distress (Levine, 2008).
